rationale: The 304-bps bid-ask spread ($6.68/$6.89) alone creates an insurmountable friction cost that would consume any realistic intraday edge before a stop is even triggered. Relative volume is only 0.15x the 20-day same-time average, confirming extremely thin participation that makes fills unreliable and exit risk high on a float of only 70,000 shares. With no news catalyst, no historical analog, and a stock that has already made a massive intraday collapse from $8.88 to $6.30 with momentum now effectively stalled in a tight low-volume chop band, there is no mechanical edge identifiable in either direction sufficient to justify the execution risk.
